title: Rethinking Language Models as Symbolic Knowledge Graphs
measurement_description: The paper measures whether language models hallucinate or exhibit social biases when querying sensitive attributes, specifically an individual's affiliation with a particular religion (Wikidata relation P140). It evaluates this by prompting models for the religion of highly unpopular entities to see if they incorrectly hallucinate an affiliation.
findings: The study found that language models generally struggle with hallucinating sensitive features like religion when queried about unpopular entities. However, larger language models, particularly GPT-4, exhibit marked improvements and heightened resilience to social biases compared to smaller baseline models. GPT-4 performed especially well on the 'Religion' relation pattern, achieving an accuracy score of roughly 85% in not hallucinating incorrect religious affiliations.
